jobs.title: Vice President Finance
jobs.description:
Your Partners in Recruitment!

Thorek/Scott and Partners (TSP) has been connecting accomplished organizations with talented individuals for almost four decades. At TSP, our track record of successfully completing challenging searches across the professional spectrum has earned us an exceptional reputation at the forefront of the recruitment industry. Our Canadian and International clients include: global banks and non-bank financial institutions, private equity and investment funds, professional service firms, and entrepreneurial businesses in a variety of industries. We value the human connection and distinguish ourselves through an unwavering dedication to understanding the goals and motivations of our clients and candidates alike.

This open role is currently being featured by Thorek/Scott and Partners! We highlight a variety of open roles every week. If you save this position to apply to later, it may appear closed when you revisit it. For a full list of all open positions, please visit www.thorekscott.com.

Position Overview

Our client is a highly successful Canadian asset management firm with an expansive global and national platform. The firm invests in a variety of long-lived asset classes through a growing portfolio of private funds and publicly listed operating entities.

They are currently seeking a Vice President, Finance to lead a growing team focused on their private investments strategy. Reporting to the SVP, the VP will drive investment finance and reporting for a set of large and complex existing and emerging funds. The role is highly visible, with extensive cross-functional interaction with senior executives and a range of complex challenges. Experience in a complex, substantive fund environment is essential for success in this role.

This is an attractive opportunity for a seasoned CPA with extensive fund operations leadership to make their mark in a growth-oriented investor with significant upward mobility.

Role Responsibilities

Own the overall fund strategy and lead finance and operations teams.
Interpret fund results, anticipate financial and operational risks, and present quarterly results and recommendations to senior management.
Oversee fund liquidity, cash flow forecasting, capital calls, investor distributions and fund-level compliance.
Review quarterly investor reporting under US GAAP Investment Company Accounting and IFRS, including financial statements, partners’ capital statements and remaining commitment schedules. Review fund valuations and entity-level financial reporting.
Maintain effective internal controls and audit readiness, and oversee the accuracy and timeliness of work performed by external service providers.
Serve as the senior finance partner to Investments, Investor Relations, Tax, Legal, Treasury and Portfolio Management. Advise on complex accounting issues, fund structures and new acquisitions.
Develop the fund finance team and improve reporting, systems and processes as the platform grows, including through the use of AI and other emerging technologies.
Respond to investor inquiries on fund performance, reporting and capital activity.
Review legal-entity accounting packages, including tax financials.
Assess how fund legal structures affect the movement of cash between entities and the consolidation of financial results.

Desired Qualifications

At least 10 years of progressive experience in finance and/or accounting, with hands-on fund experience. Private funds experience, investment management industry knowledge and exposure to complex ownership structures are assets.
University degree and a professional accounting designation (CPA/CA or equivalent).
Strong technical accounting expertise in US GAAP Investment Company Accounting and IFRS, with experience reviewing investor reporting, fund valuations and complex consolidations.
Experience overseeing fund operations, including liquidity management, forecasting, capital calls, investor distributions and fund-level compliance.
Demonstrated leadership and initiative, with the ability to develop finance teams, improve processes and partner with senior stakeholders across Investments, Investor Relations, Tax, Legal and Treasury.
Experience overseeing external service providers and working with auditors to maintain effective internal controls and audit readiness.
Strong financial systems skills, including advanced Excel. Experience with Mercatus, Workiva or Anaplan is an asset.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational and communication skills, with the judgment to anticipate risks and advise senior management.
Proactive and accountable, with the ability to manage competing priorities, adapt quickly and meet deadlines in a complex, fast-paced environment.

Please note that at present, legal eligibility to work in Canada is a prerequisite for this role.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Financial Crime
jobs.description:
Description

Build the future with us

Are you passionate about fighting financial crime and eager to contribute to the purpose of a company committed to ensuring its clients feel confident and secure about their future? As Senior Director, Financial Crime, you will play a key role in shaping the vision, performance, and transformation of iA Financial Group’s financial crime programs. Reporting to the Vice-President and Chief Compliance Officer, who also serves as the Chief Anti-Money Laundering Officer, you will lead the teams of professionals within the Anti-Money Laundering Office and the Fraud Prevention Office, while also acting as Deputy Chief Anti-Money Laundering Officer.

You will also provide functional leadership to the Chief Anti-Money Laundering Officers of the Group’s subsidiaries and mobilize AML-ATF representatives across the business sectors in managing cases and information requests. This position represents a great opportunity to showcase your skills and fully realize your potential within a caring and trustworthy company. Here, people and their development are at the heart of our priorities, creating an environment that fosters collaboration and innovation.

______________________________________________________________________________

What You’ll Accomplish With Us

As Senior Director, Financial Crime
, you will be at the heart of our mission. Your key responsibilities will include:

Lead and mobilize two teams of specialized professionals, develop expertise, and build a recognized centre of expertise across the Group.
Define the multi-year vision, risk appetite, and investment priorities related to financial crime.
Lead iA Alerte by defining the vision, roadmap, and success criteria for an integrated financial crime detection capability aimed at enhancing detection tools through the integration of artificial intelligence.
Lead the Group’s AML-ATF governance by guiding the subsidiaries’ Chief Anti-Money Laundering Officers in applying Group standards, ensuring program consistency, and supporting their accountability.
Mobilize business sectors and coordinate investigations and remediation activities while ensuring rigorous and consistent practices.
Provide strategic leadership, guide senior management decision-making, and foster alignment among business sectors and subsidiaries with the Group’s financial crime priorities.
Represent the organization and lead discussions with FINTRAC, the AMF, OSFI, and law enforcement agencies, while demonstrating the robustness of the organization’s programs and controls.

______________________________________________________________________________

What Could Accelerate Your Success In This Role

We are looking for someone who:

Is recognized for their engaging leadership and ability to inspire and rally multidisciplinary teams around a shared vision, as well as exert significant influence without direct reporting authority.
Stands out for their strategic vision, strong execution skills, and ability to turn ambition into a comprehensive operating model encompassing governance, processes, tools, and performance indicators.
Demonstrates excellent communication and influencing skills, with the ability to explain complex issues to the Board, senior management, and regulatory authorities, as well as sound judgment when managing matters with significant regulatory and reputational implications.
Has a strong interest in innovation and artificial intelligence, along with the ability to leverage emerging technologies to advance prevention, detection, and analytical practices.
Holds a bachelor’s degree in law, business administration, finance, accounting, criminology, risk management, or a related field.
Has 10 years of relevant experience, including 5 years of management experience, as well as substantial experience in financial crime, AML-ATF, fraud, compliance, or investigations within a regulated environment, including several years managing teams of professionals.
Has training or certification in AML-ATF, fraud, compliance, risk management, audit, or data, which is considered a strong asset.
Advanced proficiency in both French and English is required, as the successful candidate will regularly be responsible for managing files and information requests, coordinating investigations and remediation efforts, and communicating complex issues in a clear and accessible manner to subsidiaries, business units, senior management, and regulatory authorities.

______________________________________________________________________________

Why you’ll love working with us

A work environment where learning and development come together with a collective pursuit of excellence.
Artificial intelligence is in everyone’s hands, helping increase personal effectiveness and supporting the organization’s growth.
A healthy, safe, equitable, and inclusive environment where everyone can reach their full potential and develop freely.
The opportunity to work in a hybrid environment supported by flexibility and access to inspiring and innovative workspaces.

______________________________________________________________________________

Competitive Benefits

Flexible group insurance
Competitive pension plan
Employee share purchase plan
Vacation, wellness, and personal development days
Telemedicine
Employee and Family Assistance Program
Ergonomic furniture program
Performance bonus
Discounts on iA products
And much more!

______________________________________________________________________________

Apply now and take the lead in your career, where your talent truly matters!

______________________________________________________________________________

Hesitant to apply?

At iA, we believe in potential and value diverse experiences. If this role inspires you, we encourage you to apply. Your place may be with us, and we want to get to know you!

jobs.title: VP of Finance & Accounting (WHL Group & Family Office)
jobs.description:
About the role
WHL Group is hiring a VP of Finance & Accounting to run the finance and accounting function for a privately held, owner-led group and its Family Office. You will own the close, consolidation, treasury, cash forecasting, FP&A, tax compliance and advisor management, and lead a lean team: the Corporate Controller and two accountants.
Our CFO has moved into a combined CFO/COO role focused on operations and growth. We need a finance leader who can take the function off her plate and run it independently. This is a junior-CFO hire with a clear path to accelerated promotion to CFO, based on performance.
About WHL Group.
WHL is a group of nine entities across Canada, the United States and Barbados, reporting in CAD, USD and BBD, with a September 30 fiscal year end. It includes operating healthcare businesses, holding and management companies, and the owner's Family Office. Books are kept in QuickBooks Online.
What you'll do
Close and reporting:
run a calendarized month-end close and multi-currency consolidation for nine entities, and deliver the monthly owner reporting package and the September 30 year end
FP&A:
lead the annual budget, rolling forecasts, KPI models and variance commentary, and partner with operating leaders on results, pricing and cost
Treasury and cash:
own banking, cash positioning, intercompany funding, FX and the rolling 13-week cash forecast
Tax and compliance:
own the compliance calendar across Canada, the US and Barbados, and lead responses to tax authority reviews with external advisors
Intercompany:
keep intercompany balances reconciled and aligned with the group's transfer pricing position
Family Office:
maintain the owner's personal holdings records, draws and funding, and coordinate with personal advisors
Controls and systems:
keep every entity audit-ready and own the QuickBooks structure, close checklists and review standards
Leadership:
lead the Corporate Controller and two accountants, and manage all external finance advisors to scope, budget and deadline

The pace.
This is a high-demand, fast-paced role with overlapping deadlines and same-day or next-day owner requests that must be right the first time. We expect you to make finance decisions yourself and bring conclusions, not questions.
What you bring
CPA (CPA Canada or US CPA) or equivalent designation
12+ years in finance and accounting, including 5+ years as VP Finance, Director of Finance, Corporate Controller or equivalent in a multi-entity group
A track record of running a finance function with little oversight and hitting every close and filing deadline
Hands-on multi-entity, multi-currency consolidation, budgeting and 13-week cash forecasting
Strong Canadian corporate and indirect tax compliance knowledge, and experience with tax authority reviews
Expert QuickBooks Online across multiple company files, and advanced Excel
Experience leading a lean, hands-on accounting team, including remote staff
The judgment and presence to be an owner's trusted finance voice, and the ambition to become CFO

Nice to have:
Family Office experience; US and Barbados or Caribbean cross-border experience; transfer pricing knowledge; owner-managed or private-equity-backed background; healthcare finance; public accounting experience.
Position details
Reports to:
CFO/COO
Direct report:
Corporate Controller
Location:
Canada or United States (remote)
Type:
Full-time, permanent
Compensation:
Base salary CAD $175,000-$200,000
Career path:
Accelerated promotion to CFO, based on performance

To apply,
send your resume and a short note on the most complex multi-entity finance function you have run, and what you took off your CFO's or owner's plate.

jobs.title: Finance Director, Poultry Operations
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Opportunity:

Maple Leaf Foods is seeking a Director, Poultry Operations (Finance)
to provide financial leadership and strategic business partnership across our Poultry Operations portfolio.

This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for an experienced Finance professional who combines strong financial acumen with a deep understanding of manufacturing operations. As a key member of the Poultry Finance team, you will work closely with Poultry Operations leaders to drive financial performance, influence operational decisions and identify opportunities to improve profitability, productivity and capital efficiency.

Leading a team of 6 Finance Business Partners supporting multiple manufacturing facilities, you will be accountable for providing a clear financial perspective on business performance, challenging assumptions and ensuring that operational decisions are supported by rigorous financial analysis and sound business judgment.

The successful candidate will be a collaborative and influential leader who thrives in a complex and fast paced manufacturing environment, brings a continuous improvement mindset and is passionate about developing high-performing teams.

Any MLF team member interested in being considered for this role are encouraged to apply online by November 23, 2026. Applications received beyond that date are not guaranteed consideration.

Reason for vacancy: Existing Headcount

Snapshot Of a Day-in-the-Life

Strategic Finance Leadership & Business Partnership

Act as a trusted strategic advisor to Poultry Operations leadership, providing financial insight, constructive challenge and recommendations that support business priorities.
Lead financial performance oversight across a multi-plant portfolio, with a focus on profitability, yield, labour, productivity, inventory and capital performance.
Partner with operational leaders to evaluate strategic priorities, investment decisions, operational risks and opportunities to improve financial results.
Lead and develop a team of Finance Business Partner Managers, ensuring consistent, high-quality financial support and strong alignment with operational priorities.

Operational Performance & Financial Outlook

Own the consolidated financial outlook for the Poultry Operations portfolio, ensuring operational developments, emerging risks and improvement opportunities are reflected in financial expectations.
Review and challenge financial and operational performance, identifying key drivers, performance gaps and opportunities to improve business outcomes.
Oversee scenario modelling, financial impact assessments and trade-off analysis to support complex operational, productivity and capital decisions.
Evaluate proposed operational improvement initiatives and capital investments, providing recommendations on financial returns, risks and expected outcomes.
Monitor the financial performance of approved initiatives, ensuring expected benefits are tracked and opportunities for corrective action are identified.
Partner with plant Finance and cross-functional teams to understand the financial implications of changes in yield, labour, overhead, inventory, product costs and capital requirements.

People Leadership & Continuous Improvement

Build, coach and develop a high-performing team of Finance Business Partners, fostering accountability, collaboration and strong business-partnering capabilities.
Establish consistent performance measures, analytical approaches and financial decision-support practices across the Poultry Operations portfolio.
Prioritize Finance resources and analytical efforts toward the most material business risks, performance opportunities and value-creation initiatives.
Promote an integrated Finance support model that enables effective collaboration across Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and other business functions.
Drive continuous improvement in financial analysis, reporting effectiveness and operational decision support.

Qualifications

What You’ll Bring:

Progressive Finance experience, including significant leadership experience in a manufacturing, operations Finance or business-partnering environment.
Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, cost structures, productivity drivers, inventory management and capital investment analysis.
Demonstrated ability to lead financial performance and provide strategic direction across a complex, multi-site or multi-business environment.
Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities, with the ability to translate complex operational and financial information into clear, actionable recommendations.
Proven ability to influence senior leaders, constructively challenge assumptions and drive alignment across cross-functional teams.
Experience leading, coaching and developing high-performing Finance teams.
Exceptional communication, relationship-management and executive presentation skills.
A proactive, results-oriented mindset with a passion for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Experience in food manufacturing, protein processing or poultry operations would be considered a strong asset.
A professional accounting designation (CPA) or equivalent relevant education and experience would be an asset.
Enter text

Additional Information

What We Offer At Maple Leaf Foods

Being part of a high-performance, people-focused company that has an inspiring and unique vision to become the most sustainable protein company on earth, and a deep commitment to sustainable protein across North America.
An inclusive company culture and a work environment that keeps our people safe, rewards excellence, and empowers everyone to learn and contribute their best.
Competitive Health and Wellness benefits that offer flexibility to meet your individual or family needs, including programs focused on improving mental health and wellbeing. These benefits start on your first day of employment.
Defined Contribution Pension Plan with company matching that starts on your first day of employment.
Learning and development opportunities, including workshops, ‘speaker series’ events, and resources that allow you to develop your skills and progress your career.
Comprehensive tuition reimbursement program that supports continuous learning and development of our team members through investment in eligible degrees, diplomas, professional certification, or trades programs.
Supporting our deep commitment to community impact, we offer up to two paid days annually to volunteer at a cause of your choice.

Company Description

About Us:

We’re a carbon neutral food company on a purposeful journey to Raise the Good in Food through better nutrition, safer food and workplaces, more humane animal care, and environmental sustainability efforts that protect our planet. We care about our communities and commit to reducing food insecurity in Canada. Join us on the journey. Let’s build a better future, together.

We’re passionate about food. For more than 100 years, we’ve made delicious, healthy protein that Canadians love under iconic national and regional brands, like Maple Leaf®, Schneiders®, and Greenfield Natural Meat Co.® We’re on a journey to become the most sustainable protein company – not just in Canada – but on earth.

We are carbon neutral.

We are one of the only food companies in Canada to set science-based targets.

We’re a global food company with approximately 10,000 team members. We operate sites in 20+ locations across Canada. We also have locations in the U.S. and Mexico, and do business in Asia.

A Diverse And Inclusive Work Environment

Championing diversity and inclusion is a critical component to advancing our collective purpose and vision and living the Maple Leaf Leadership Values. We believe in building, investing in, recognizing, and rewarding remarkable people who value an inclusive workplace, embrace all forms of diversity, and commit to including every voice in our collaborative environment. We’re so much stronger when we know we’re accepted and valued for who we are and what we each bring to the workplace.

We embrace a strong, values-based culture

Our eight Leadership Values are our north star. They guide the decisions we make for all our stakeholders: our consumers, our customers, our people, our communities, our shareholders, and the environment.

Doing What’s Right
Shared Value
High Performance
Diverse and Inclusive Teams
Disciplined Decision Making
Our Accountability
Intense Curiosity
Transparency and Humility

We thank all applicants for their interest in exploring employment opportunities with Maple Leaf Foods; however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Applicants may be subject to a background check and must meet the security criteria designated for the position.

Championing diversity and inclusion is a critical component to advancing our collective purpose and vision, living the Maple Leaf Leadership Values, and delivering winning results. Accommodation is available upon request for applicants with disabilities in the recruitment and assessment process and when hired; please contact our Talent Attraction Team at accommodations@mapleleaf.com.

Disclaimer: Please note that salaries posted on sites other than the MLF Careers Page are not a reflection of Maple Leaf Foods and are an estimated salary range provided by that particular job board. Maple Leaf Foods offers competitive wages and an attractive total rewards package, which will be discussed during an interview with our Talent Team.

jobs.title: Director Corporate Finance
jobs.description:
Director Corporate Finance

Illuminex AI is an Ontario technology company that builds practical solutions to deliver airfield intelligence. Our platform uses sensor fusion and edge computing to help airport teams detect foreign object debris, monitor perimeters, assess surface conditions, and support safer operations. We are an 11 person organization headquartered in Cobourg.

We are hiring a Finance and Corporate Support Coordinator. The core of the role is owning day to day bookkeeping, keeping financial records in excellent shape, administering payroll, and preparing and filing our annual corporate tax returns. A key responsibility is preparing and submitting our Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) claims to maximize eligible refunds. Because these financial duties do not require the full week at current scale, if full time you will also spend time assisting with corporate activities including RFQ responses, bid preparation, quote generation, and marketing writing. This is a hybrid finance and operations role suited to someone comfortable working across both areas in a small team.

Hours are flexible and can range from part time to full time depending on the candidate and the needs of the business. The role is fully remote. Preference is given to candidates based in Northern Ontario. An office in Cobourg can be provided if desired, but is not required.

Key Responsibilities

• Maintain complete and accurate books of account including day to day transactions, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and bank reconciliations.
• Prepare monthly, quarterly and year end financial statements and keep the financial records in strong condition.
• Administer payroll for our team of approximately 11 people including source deductions, remittances, and Ontario compliance.
• Prepare and file annual corporate tax returns (T2) and related schedules.
• Track and document expenditures so they support and maximize our Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credit claims. Coordinate with technical staff on proper allocation of project time and costs.
• Prepare and submit SR&ED claims, including supporting schedules, technical documentation coordination, and all required forms. Work with external advisors as needed.
• Support grant reporting with accurate cost accounting.
• Spend remaining capacity on general corporate and business development support, including assisting with marketing content, drafting and responding to Requests for Quotation (RFQs) and bids, preparing quotes, and handling other administrative tasks as needed.

Qualifications

• Proven full cycle bookkeeping experience with a Canadian small business or startup.
• Hands on experience preparing and submitting SR&ED claims is a strong asset.
• Experience preparing and filing Canadian corporate tax returns (T2) is preferred.
• Solid knowledge of Canadian payroll including Ontario rules, source deductions, and year end reporting.
• Proficiency with accounting software such as QuickBooks.
• Ability to work independently within a small remote team of about 11 people.
• Excellent attention to detail, strong written communication, and comfort moving between structured accounting work and varied corporate support tasks such as RFQ responses and quote preparation.
• Preference for candidates based in Northern Ontario.
• Authorized to work in Canada.

What We Offer

• Flexible hours that can range from part time to full time.
• Fully remote arrangement with preference for candidates in northern Ontario.
• Competitive compensation and the chance to contribute across both financial accuracy and practical business support such as RFQs, bids, and quotes, plus additional stock based compensation providing an option on the success of the business you support.
• A small team environment where you own the books and also help the company win and execute work.
• Room to grow into a more significant role as the Company scales.

Compensation

For full time candidates, a competitive base salary in the range of $68,000 to $75,000 CAD depending on experience with SR&ED claim preparation and submission, corporate tax filing, payroll, and the hybrid corporate support work.
